title: Day and Trial Passes: basis for validity-window expiration and forfeiture
content:
This document states the basis on which a Day and Trial Passes pass (Single Day Pass, Three-Day Trial Pass, Seven-Day Trial Pass, Weekly Visitor Pass, Monthly Trial Pass, Corporate Guest Pass) lapses at the end of its validity window.

## Rule
A pass lapses, and any visits not yet used on it are forfeited, once the current time is no earlier than the date the pass's validity window began, plus the tier's validity-days count of calendar days, counted as full calendar days with no partial-day rounding. A pass that has lapsed in this way is administratively archived afterward.

## Eligibility checklist
- What is checked: the company's own current record of the date the pass's validity window began, correlated to the same pass.
- When it is checked: before the lapse is recorded.
- Timing rule: the current time must be no earlier than that start date plus the tier's validity-days count of full calendar days; a check made exactly on that day still satisfies the condition (the boundary is inclusive), and a check made on any earlier day does not.

### Boundary illustration (hypothetical)
For any tier, take the date the pass's validity window began as the anchor and the tier's own validity-days count as the span. On the last calendar day of that span, the pass has not yet lapsed. On the calendar day the span completes, the pass lapses, its unused visits are forfeited, and it is administratively archived.
